chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Fadalah, from Aban, from Salamah, Abu Hafs, from Abu Abdillah, from his father, upon them be peace, who said:

The charity of al-fitr (fitrana) is due on every young and old, free or slave, for every person you support, meaning the one you spend upon on, [consisting of] a sa' of dates, or a sa' of barley, or a sa' of raisins. Then, when it was the time of Uthman, he changed it to two mudds of wheat.

key_terms.صَدَقَةُ اَلْفِطْرَةِ: Zakat al-Fitr (charity of breaking the fast)

ai.seo_question: What are the original and changed obligations for Zakat al-Fitr according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from the chain of the Ahl al-Bayt establishes the foundational obligation of Zakat al-Fitr as a purification for the fasting person, mandating a specific measure (saa') of staple foods for every dependent, regardless of age or freedom. It records the historical precedent set by Caliph Uthman ibn Affan, who substituted the original provisions with two mudds of wheat, a change widely accepted in Shia jurisprudence as a valid alternative that became the standard practice. This narration highlights the flexibility in the form of the charity while maintaining its essential purpose of supporting the needy at the end of Ramadan.
